newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia sets new date for sale of nickel stake.
newsitem.headline: Colombia sets new date for sale of nickel stake.

text.p: Signaling possible problems with the Colombian government's sale of its minority stake in Cerro Matoso SA, one of the world's largest nickel producers, a government official said Tuesday that it had been delayed by at least two months.
Finance Minister Jose Antonio Ocampo told reporters in September that the government would sell its stake in the mine, the world's fourth largest, by "no later than mid-December."
But Gabriel Borrero, head of the state-run Institute of Industrial Development, told reporters the sale date had now been rescheduled for "no later than February 28."
Borrero gave no reason for the delay, which will mean a shortfall in government privatization revenues this year.
South Africa's Gencor Ltd, which owns a 52.3 percent interest in the mine, has been mentioned among the top possible bidders for the government's 47.7 percent stake.
Ocampo has said the government hopes to receive more than $100 million from privation of the mine, which boasts an annual nickel output of about 65 million pounds.
